q: The Nekhoroshev theorem (1977) on near-integrable Hamiltonian systems provides stability over exponentially long time scales. For perturbation size ε, actions I(t) stay within O(ε^b) of I(0) for time:
opts: O(exp(1/ε^a)) for some exponents a,b > 0 depending on the number of degrees of freedom
exp: Nekhoroshev stability: under convexity conditions on H₀(I), the actions satisfy |I(t)−I(0)| ≤ Cε^b for |t| ≤ T₀ exp((ε₀/ε)^a). This super-exponential time scale bridges KAM (infinite time for Diophantine tori) and Chirikov diffusion (polynomial time for resonant zones).
